title: the three doshas as a way of noticing, not a diagnosis

segments.voice: Yesterday, the three doshas as a way of noticing, not a diagnosis, told by their qualities: dry and moving, hot and sharp, heavy and steady. Which quality kept showing up? Day one thousand two hundred eighty-eight.
screen: `A QUALITY IS LIGHTER THAN A LABEL.`

segments.voice: At the end of a checkup a doctor might say: you're healthy. It's good news, and it's mostly a list of things that aren't there. No fever. Nothing broken. Numbers in range. The classical Ayurveda texts have a definition of a healthy person too. It starts in the body, the way a checkup does, and then it keeps going and ends somewhere a blood test doesn't reach. It's also the last day of the week, so after the definition, a look back. Today: what the old texts call well.
screen: `YOU'RE HEALTHY.` → `A LIST OF WHAT ISN'T THERE.` → `A DEFINITION THAT KEEPS GOING.`

segments.voice: The Sushruta Samhita, another of Ayurveda's classical texts, gives it in one verse. In paraphrase: the one whose doshas are in balance, whose digestive fire is balanced, whose tissues and wastes do their work, and whose self, senses and mind are clear and content, that one is called svastha, healthy. Walk through it in order. Balanced doshas: what moves, what heats, what holds, none of them running wild. A balanced fire: digestion, the body's way of changing food into itself. Tissues and wastes doing their jobs: the plain plumbing of a body. And then the last line turns inward. A self, senses and mind that are prasanna: clear, settled, content. In this definition, health doesn't stop at the body. This path doesn't use the definition as a checklist to score anyone. It's a lens, like the rest of this part, and a real checkup still belongs with a doctor. But the shape is worth noticing: body first, then self, senses and mind. Now the look back over the week. It began with the Atharva Veda's healing hymns: the healer's blessed hands, a cough sent flying, plants called mothers, medicine within the waters. Then the turn to Ayurveda: the three doshas as forces, then by their qualities. And today, the word for well.
screen: `BALANCED DOSHAS, BALANCED FIRE.` · `TISSUES AND WASTES AT WORK.` · `A CLEAR SELF, SENSES AND MIND.` · `THE WEEK: HYMNS, THEN THE DOSHAS.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: check the last line of the definition, gently. Start with the senses. What can you hear right now? What can you see, even with your eyes half closed? Then the mind: is it busy or settled? No grading, just a look. Then the simplest question: is there any ease here at all, even a little? Rest with whatever is there. If you pray, you can rest in prayer here. The bell holds the time.
The three doshas, as a way of noticing, not a diagnosis. Today, balanced doshas open Sushruta's definition of svastha, healthy, and a clear, content mind closes it. Today's word.

Your line: the three doshas as a way of noticing, not a diagnosis. Today, once, after asking how your body is, ask the next question too: and how's the mind? Day one thousand two hundred eighty-eight.
